title: The Opt-In Approach
intro: Instead of converting sceptics, work with the colleagues who already value research.

learn.title: The approach
learn.text:
**Find allies** — curious or frustrated colleagues
**Start small** — a project you know will succeed
**Let it spread** — results, not declarations
**Trade up** — replace low-value work with opt-in demand
**Say no gently** — offer alternatives, be transparent

It blends bottom-up management, servant leadership and the HCI idea of user opt-in.

try.explain: Demand spreads from results, not from persuasion.

learn.title: How to find them
learn.text:
Listen in cross-functional meetings for **who asks about users** — and who **complains about customer pain**. Both are signals of someone ready to opt in.

Then choose a manageable first project with a likely, measurable win. Not the hardest problem; the one that will demonstrably work.

try.q: Which colleague is a likely ally?
options: One who complains about customer pain
One who asks for faster delivery
One who owns the largest budget
One who has used research before
try.explain: Frustration with customer problems is an opening.

learn.title: Saying no without saying no
learn.text:
Prioritise existing commitments honestly, and use opt-in demand to **retire low-value requests**.

When you have to decline: offer a lighter method, a later slot, or existing evidence. Be transparent about why.

This is the origin of his later “research as a service” model — the same idea, matured.

try.q: What should you offer when declining a request?
options: A lighter method, a later slot
A detailed explanation of your workload
A promise to revisit next quarter
try.explain: Saying no without saying no. Or existing evidence.

test.q: What is the premise of the opt-in approach?
options: Build influence with people who already want it
Run research in secret until it proves itself
test.explain: “You must teach stakeholders the value first” rarely works with executives.

test.q: What should the first project be?
options: Manageable, with a likely measurable win
The one the sceptics care about
test.explain: Visible success is the recruiting mechanism.
Let the work do the arguing.

test.q: What should opt-in demand be used to retire?
test.explain: Trading up is part of the method.
